## 【134†In std::rc】
# Struct Rc [Button: Copy item path]

1.0.0 · 【135†Source】

    `pub struct Rc<T, A = 【136†Global】>

    where
        A: 【137†Allocator】,
        T: ?【138†Sized】,

    { /* private fields */ }`

Expand description

A single-threaded reference-counting pointer. ‘Rc’ stands for ‘Reference Counted’.

See the 【134†module-level documentation】 for more details.
The inherent methods of `Rc` are all associated functions, which means that you have to call them as e.g., 【45†`Rc::get_mut(&mut value)`】 instead of `value.get_mut()`. This avoids conflicts with methods of the inner type `T`.
## Implementations【3†§】

Constructs a new `Rc<T>`.

##### 【143†§】Examples

    `use std::rc::Rc;

    let five = Rc::new(5);`

1.60.0 · 【144†Source】
#### pub fn 【5†new_cyclic】<F>(data_fn: F) -> 【141†Rc】<T>

where F: 【145†FnOnce】(&【146†Weak】<T>) -> T,

Constructs a new `Rc<T>` while giving you a `Weak<T>` to the allocation, to allow you to construct a `T` which holds a weak pointer to itself.
Generally, a structure circularly referencing itself, either directly or indirectly, should not hold a strong reference to itself to prevent a memory leak. Using this function, you get access to the weak pointer during the initialization of `T`, before the `Rc<T>` is created, such that you can clone and store it inside the `T`.
`new_cyclic` first allocates the managed allocation for the `Rc<T>`, then calls your closure, giving it a `Weak<T>` to this allocation, and only afterwards completes the construction of the `Rc<T>` by placing the `T` returned from your closure into the allocation.

Since the new `Rc<T>` is not fully-constructed until `Rc<T>::new_cyclic` returns, calling 【147†`upgrade`】 on the weak reference inside your closure will fail and result in a `None` value.
##### 【148†§】Panics

If `data_fn` panics, the panic is propagated to the caller, and the temporary 【146†`Weak<T>`】 is dropped normally.
##### 【149†§】Examples

    `use std::rc::{Rc, Weak};

    struct Gadget {
        me: Weak<Gadget>,
    }

    impl Gadget {
        /// Constructs a reference counted Gadget.
        fn new() -> Rc<Self> {
            // `me` is a `Weak<Gadget>` pointing at the new allocation of the
            // `Rc` we're constructing.
            Rc::new_cyclic(|me| {
                // Create the actual struct here.
                Gadget { me: me.clone() }
            })
        }
        /// Returns a reference counted pointer to Self.
        fn me(&self) -> Rc<Self> {
            self.me.upgrade().unwrap()
        }
    }`
1.82.0 · 【150†Source】
#### pub fn 【6†new_uninit】() -> 【141†Rc】<【151†MaybeUninit】<T>>

Constructs a new `Rc` with uninitialized contents.

##### 【152†§】Examples

    `use std::rc::Rc;

    let mut five = Rc::<u32>::new_uninit();

    // Deferred initialization:
    Rc::get_mut(&mut five).unwrap().write(5);

    let five = unsafe { five.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*five, 5)`

1.92.0 · 【153†Source】
#### pub fn 【7†new_zeroed】() -> 【141†Rc】<【151†MaybeUninit】<T>>

Constructs a new `Rc` with uninitialized contents, with the memory being filled with `0` bytes.

See 【154†`MaybeUninit::zeroed`】 for examples of correct and incorrect usage of this method.

##### 【155†§】Examples

    `use std::rc::Rc;

    let zero = Rc::<u32>::new_zeroed();
    let zero = unsafe { zero.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*zero, 0)`

【167†Source】
#### pub fn 【12†map】<U>(this: 【141†Rc】<T>, f: impl 【145†FnOnce】(【168†&T】) -> U) -> 【141†Rc】<U>

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`smart_pointer_try_map` 【169†#144419†github.com】)

Maps the value in an `Rc`, reusing the allocation if possible.

`f` is called on a reference to the value in the `Rc`, and the result is returned, also in an `Rc`.
Note: this is an associated function, which means that you have to call it as `Rc::map(r, f)` instead of `r.map(f)`. This is so that there is no conflict with a method on the inner type.
##### 【170†§】Examples

    `#![feature(smart_pointer_try_map)]

    use std::rc::Rc;

    let r = Rc::new(7);
    let new = Rc::map(r, |i| i + 7);
    assert_eq!(*new, 14);`

【171†Source】
#### pub fn 【13†try_map】<R>( this: 【141†Rc】<T>, f: impl 【145†FnOnce】(【168†&T】) -> R, ) -> <<R as 【172†Try】>::【173†Residual】 as 【174†Residual】<【141†Rc】<<R as 【172†Try】>::【175†Output】>>>::【176†TryType】

where R: 【172†Try】, <R as 【172†Try】>::【173†Residual】: 【174†Residual】<【141†Rc】<<R as 【172†Try】>::【175†Output】>>,

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`smart_pointer_try_map` 【169†#144419†github.com】)

Attempts to map the value in an `Rc`, reusing the allocation if possible.
`f` is called on a reference to the value in the `Rc`, and if the operation succeeds, the result is returned, also in an `Rc`.

Note: this is an associated function, which means that you have to call it as `Rc::try_map(r, f)` instead of `r.try_map(f)`. This is so that there is no conflict with a method on the inner type.
##### 【177†§】Examples

    `#![feature(smart_pointer_try_map)]

    use std::rc::Rc;

    let b = Rc::new(7);
    let new = Rc::try_map(b, |&i| u32::try_from(i)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(*new, 7);`

【186†Source】
#### pub fn 【17†new_cyclic_in】<F>(data_fn: F, alloc: A) -> 【141†Rc】<T, A>

where F: 【145†FnOnce】(&【146†Weak】<T, A>) -> T,

🔬This is a nightly-only experimental API. (`allocator_api` 【159†#32838†github.com】)

Constructs a new `Rc<T, A>` in the given allocator while giving you a `Weak<T, A>` to the allocation, to allow you to construct a `T` which holds a weak pointer to itself.
Generally, a structure circularly referencing itself, either directly or indirectly, should not hold a strong reference to itself to prevent a memory leak. Using this function, you get access to the weak pointer during the initialization of `T`, before the `Rc<T, A>` is created, such that you can clone and store it inside the `T`.
`new_cyclic_in` first allocates the managed allocation for the `Rc<T, A>`, then calls your closure, giving it a `Weak<T, A>` to this allocation, and only afterwards completes the construction of the `Rc<T, A>` by placing the `T` returned from your closure into the allocation.

Since the new `Rc<T, A>` is not fully-constructed until `Rc<T, A>::new_cyclic_in` returns, calling 【147†`upgrade`】 on the weak reference inside your closure will fail and result in a `None` value.
##### 【187†§】Panics

If `data_fn` panics, the panic is propagated to the caller, and the temporary 【146†`Weak<T, A>`】 is dropped normally.

##### 【188†§】Examples

See 【5†`new_cyclic`】.

1.4.0 · 【196†Source】
#### pub fn 【22†try_unwrap】(this: 【141†Rc】<T, A>) -> 【157†Result】<T, 【141†Rc】<T, A>>

Returns the inner value, if the `Rc` has exactly one strong reference.

Otherwise, an 【197†`Err`】 is returned with the same `Rc` that was passed in.

This will succeed even if there are outstanding weak references.
##### 【198†§】Examples

    `use std::rc::Rc;

    let x = Rc::new(3);
    assert_eq!(Rc::try_unwrap(x), Ok(3));

    let x = Rc::new(4);
    let _y = Rc::clone(&x);
    assert_eq!(*Rc::try_unwrap(x).unwrap_err(), 4);`

1.70.0 · 【199†Source】
#### pub fn 【23†into_inner】(this: 【141†Rc】<T, A>) -> 【200†Option】<T>

Returns the inner value, if the `Rc` has exactly one strong reference.

Otherwise, 【201†`None`】 is returned and the `Rc` is dropped.

This will succeed even if there are outstanding weak references.

If `Rc::into_inner` is called on every clone of this `Rc`, it is guaranteed that exactly one of the calls returns the inner value. This means in particular that the inner value is not dropped.
【22†`Rc::try_unwrap`】 is conceptually similar to `Rc::into_inner`. And while they are meant for different use-cases, `Rc::into_inner(this)` is in fact equivalent to `【22†Rc::try_unwrap】(this).【202†ok】()`. (Note that the same kind of equivalence does not hold true for 【203†`Arc`】, due to race conditions that do not apply to `Rc`!)
##### 【204†§】Examples

    `use std::rc::Rc;

    let x = Rc::new(3);
    assert_eq!(Rc::into_inner(x), Some(3));

    let x = Rc::new(4);
    let y = Rc::clone(&x);

    assert_eq!(Rc::into_inner(y), None);
    assert_eq!(Rc::into_inner(x), Some(4));`

【205†Source】【206†§】

### impl<T> 【141†Rc】<【207†[T]】>

1.82.0 · 【208†Source】

#### pub fn 【24†new_uninit_slice】(len: 【209†usize】) -> 【141†Rc】<[【151†MaybeUninit】<T>]>

Constructs a new reference-counted slice with uninitialized contents.
##### 【210†§】Examples

    `use std::rc::Rc;

    let mut values = Rc::<[u32]>::new_uninit_slice(3);

    // Deferred initialization:
    let data = Rc::get_mut(&mut values).unwrap();
    data[0].write(1);
    data[1].write(2);
    data[2].write(3);

    let values = unsafe { values.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*values, [1, 2, 3])`

1.92.0 · 【211†Source】
#### pub fn 【25†new_zeroed_slice】(len: 【209†usize】) -> 【141†Rc】<[【151†MaybeUninit】<T>]>

Constructs a new reference-counted slice with uninitialized contents, with the memory being filled with `0` bytes.

See 【154†`MaybeUninit::zeroed`】 for examples of correct and incorrect usage of this method.
##### 【212†§】Examples

    `use std::rc::Rc;

    let values = Rc::<[u32]>::new_zeroed_slice(3);
    let values = unsafe { values.assume_init() };

    assert_eq!(*values, [0, 0, 0])`

#### pub fn 【26†new_uninit_slice_in】(len: 【209†usize】, alloc: A) -> 【141†Rc】<[【151†MaybeUninit】<T>], A>

Constructs a new reference-counted slice with uninitialized contents.
